back: Individuals better suited to their environment are more likely to survive and reproduce, passing on their alleles.
Variation → over-production → struggle for survival (competition) → better adapted survive and reproduce → pass on alleles → over many generations, alleles become more common.
The change in the adaptive features of a population over time as a result of natural selection.
The process, resulting from natural selection, by which populations become more suited to their environment over many generations.
Random mutation gives resistance; the antibiotic kills non-resistant bacteria; the resistant ones survive and reproduce by binary fission.

front: How can antibiotic resistance be slowed?
back: Use antibiotics only when needed (not for viral infections), complete the course, never share or save them.

front: Examples of natural selection happening now?
back: Antibiotic-resistant bacteria (such as some TB strains), insecticide-resistant mosquitoes, chloroquine-resistant malaria parasites.
Choose parents with the wanted feature → breed them → select the best offspring → repeat for many generations.

front: How was the Tuli breed of cattle produced?
back: By selective breeding, from the 1940s, of hardy local cattle in southern Zimbabwe, for hardiness, fertility and good beef.
Natural: the environment selects features for survival; slow. Artificial: humans select features useful to them; faster; reduces genetic variation.
